RFC5549-4-1.note: Superseded row restating RFC8950-4-1; same judgement. Sentence: MUST only advertise IPv4 or VPN-IPv4 NLRI with an IPv6 next hop after ascertaining peer support for the relevant AFI/SAFI pair. Now proven on next-hop-self resolution: TestRFC8950IPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair drives Peer.resolveNextHop with ExtNH for 1/1 only, 1/128 only and neither, asserting the IPv6 address only for the licensed pair and ErrNextHopIncompatible with no address otherwise, so the VPN-IPv4 and per-pair clauses are covered. Still unproven: (a) an explicit next hop -- resolveNextHop returns NextHopExplicit unchecked ('validated by the wire builder'), and UpdateBuilder emits MP_REACH with the given next hop for any non-unicast SAFI (message/update_build.go) with no ExtNH test, so an explicit IPv6 next hop for VPN-IPv4 without the pair negotiated has no unit that would go red; (b) a forwarded route whose IPv6 next hop is left unchanged toward a peer lacking the pair. No unit builds or inspects an UPDATE.

RFC5549-4-2.note: Sentence: MUST use RFC 5492 Capability Advertisement with the Extended Next Hop Encoding capability to establish whether the peer supports this for the NLRI AFI/SAFI pair(s). The 4-2-tagged units (TestExtendedNextHopCapability, TestExtendedNextHopRoundTrip) prove only the capability TLV encodes and parses. The clause 'to establish whether its peer supports this' (support decided from the peer's advertised capability) has no 4-2-tagged assertion; the negotiation units that would prove it carry only 4-1 and RFC8950 tags.

RFC5549-4-3.note: Forbidden: a Capability Code other than 5 for Extended Next Hop Encoding. Red on it: TestCapabilityCodeConstants asserts uint8(CodeExtendedNextHop)==5, and TestExtendedNextHopCapability requires a raw code-0x05 TLV to parse as *ExtendedNextHop (require.True on the type assertion). Single-polarity marker on the row.

RFC5549-5-1.note: Forbidden: a route reflector changing the encoding of a next hop it passes along unchanged. Red on it: require.Equal(mpReach, attrs[14]) and the next-hop byte compare in TestReactorForwardRRPreservesExtendedNextHop, which reflects a 16-byte IPv6 next hop for IPv4 NLRI through the reactor forward path. Single-polarity marker on the row.
